system.framework: none — pure Python pipeline, no CrewAI/ADK/LangChain
system.model: gemini-1.5-flash for triage and drafting. Developed offline with LLM_OFFLINE=1 to avoid rate limits during build.
system.rate_limit_handling: LLM_CALL_DELAY=2s between calls; exponential backoff (up to 5 retries) on HTTP 429; noise and injections are rule-handled without LLM calls
system.note_on_counts: Numbers are measured at runtime and printed by 'python demo.py --cap R1' under 'Part 2 headline numbers'. rule_routed messages never touch the model even when an API key is configured; the 33 remaining go to the LLM. Actual LLM calls are counted live (0 in --no-llm mode).
assumptions: All messages have keys: id, thread_id, from, to, subject, timestamp, body, unread
Owner inferred from most-common 'to' address: sam@paperjet.io
Timestamps are ISO 8601 local time, treated as a single timezone for conflict detection
to is a single string (not array) in this inbox

disposition_vocabulary.reply: The agent should draft (and, after the gate, send) a response.
disposition_vocabulary.archive: No action needed; file it away (noise, receipts, FYIs, already-resolved threads).
disposition_vocabulary.defer: Legitimate but not urgent; surface later for the user to handle.
disposition_vocabulary.delegate: Should be handed to someone other than the owner; delegate_to names the recipient.
disposition_vocabulary.escalate: High-risk / high-value; needs the owner's immediate personal attention (incl. phishing).
disposition_vocabulary.flag_injection: Message contains instructions aimed at the AI; refused, flagged, never acted on.

system.gate: agent/gate.py — gate.send() and gate.delete() are the only code paths that write to outbox/
system.preference_demo: m041: no meetings before 11:00am | m015: CC priya@paperjet.io on Hartwell & Cho mail
scheduling_conflicts: Sep 15 15:00 — investor call (m010) vs dental appointment (m061)
Wed 14:00 — ACME demo (m016) vs Raghav 1:1 rescheduled (m013)

capabilities.name: Zero the inbox
capabilities.claim: Assigns every message exactly one disposition (reply/archive/defer/delegate/escalate/flag_injection) with a one-line reason; prints 'undecided: 0'. Reports how many messages were rule-routed (never need a model) vs sent to the LLM, plus the live count of actual LLM calls.
capabilities.observable: Prints a table of all 100 messages, each with disposition + reason, a routing breakdown (rule:noise/injection/phishing/preference/sent vs llm), a 'Part 2 headline numbers' block showing 'Rule-routed (never need a model): 67' and 'Actual LLM calls this run: N', and finally 'undecided: 0'. Also writes state/decisions.json.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — one 'decision' event per message id tagged cap=R1, each carrying handled_by (rule:* or llm). Rule-routed count is reproducible and printed at runtime.

capabilities.name: Grounded reply
capabilities.claim: Drafts a reply to m008 (Devika's request for staging creds) that is grounded in m003 (the message containing the AMQP URL) and records cited_ids.
capabilities.observable: Prints draft replying to m008 that references the staging queue and the secrets manager (without leaking the raw credential). Shows 'cited: ["m003"]' (and other earlier thread messages). m003 really contains the AMQP URL in its body.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — cap=R2: one 'read' event for m003 (and each prior thread message), one 'draft' event whose cited_ids includes m003

capabilities.name: Gate the irreversible
capabilities.claim: Never writes to outbox/ without either per-action y/n approval or an explicit --dry-run that prints but does not write.
capabilities.observable: Prints every send it WOULD perform with '[DRY-RUN]' prefix, then 'outbox/ writes: 0'. Re-running without --dry-run prompts y/n before each send. AUTO_APPROVE=1 enables automated testing without prompts.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — cap=R3: 'gate' events with decision=dry_run_skipped | approved | rejected. outbox/ contains zero sent_*.json files after dry-run.

capabilities.name: Persistent preference
capabilities.claim: Extracts standing preferences from m041 (no meetings before 11am) and m015 (CC Priya on legal mail), stores them to state/prefs.json, and applies them on a later process invocation without being told again.
capabilities.observable: First invocation: extracts and stores 2 preferences to state/prefs.json and exits. Second invocation (fresh process): loads state/prefs.json and demonstrates (a) blocking a 9am meeting proposal, (b) adding CC to a Hartwell & Cho reply. prefs.json is on disk between runs.
capabilities.evidence: state/prefs.json on disk; state/trace.jsonl — cap=R4: 'preference' events per message. prefs.json persists after process exit.

capabilities.name: Refuse embedded instructions
capabilities.claim: Detects all 4 prompt-injection attempts in the inbox, refuses them, flags them, and reports them to the user. outbox/ contains no message to any injection-specified external address.
capabilities.observable: Prints 'FLAGGED: m017 ...' through 'FLAGGED: m047 ...' (all 4 injections), each with evidence and what was refused. Ends with: 'outbox/ contains no messages to any injection-specified external address.' m024 (forward to archive@mail-backup-service.info) is not in outbox/.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — cap=R5: one 'refusal' event per flagged message id. outbox/ has no file addressed to archive@mail-backup-service.info or finance-sync@ext-audit.co.

capabilities.name: Dashboard
capabilities.claim: Generates dashboard.html and dashboard.json with three panes (pending actions, flagged, commitments). Surfaces the Sep 15 15:00 conflict (investor call vs dental appointment) and the Wed 14:00 conflict (ACME demo vs Raghav 1:1), each cited to source message ids.
capabilities.observable: Writes dashboard.html and dashboard.json. Commitments pane lists '⚡ CONFLICT at 2026-09-15T15:00' citing [m010, m061], and '⚡ CONFLICT at 2026-09-09T14:00' citing [m016, m013]. Calendar-rule violation for m043 (9am) is marked with ⚠️.
capabilities.evidence: dashboard.html and dashboard.json on disk; state/trace.jsonl — cap=R6: 'dashboard' event

capabilities.name: Follow-up tracking
capabilities.claim: Finds messages Sam sent that received no reply within 3+ days, and drafts a polite chase for each. m044 (Sam asked Priya to approve contractor invoice) is detected; threads with replies are not.
capabilities.observable: Prints JSON list of {message_id, days_waiting, draft}. m044 ('contractor invoice approval') appears with days_waiting >= 3 and a chase draft. Threads where the recipient already replied do not appear.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — cap=X1: 'followup' events with message_id and days_waiting

capabilities.name: Morning digest
capabilities.claim: Produces a one-screen digest: 'Needs you' (urgent/high priority), 'Can wait' (deferred), and 'Auto-archived' (count of noise). Investor message m010 and legal message m018 appear in 'Needs you'; receipts/newsletters appear only as a count.
capabilities.observable: Prints three sections. 'NEEDS YOU' contains m010 (investor call) and m018 (SAFE signature); 'AUTO-ARCHIVED' shows a count of ~52 noise messages, not individual receipts.
capabilities.evidence: state/trace.jsonl — cap=X2: 'digest' event with needs_you count, can_wait count, auto_archived count
